metadata.title: BiteCheck: Do Claude's API Tests Actually Catch Bugs?
metadata.author: Omkar Salian
metadata.persona: Omkar Salian (first person; synthetic Kokoro voice)

beats.narration_text: Claude can draft a whole suite of API tests that all come back green. But a green test only means something if it would turn red when the code is wrong. BiteCheck tells an engineer reviewing AI written tests which ones would catch a broken business rule.

shot.visual_intent: A crate of test pages drops in; check marks pop on each page; a question mark appears beside the crate.
shot.motion_claim: A crate of test pages drops in; check marks pop on each page; a question mark appears beside the crate.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: It's called BiteCheck. When it's done, it will be a public GitHub repository with four parts: a prompt that tells Claude how to write the tests, a list of bugs I put into the code on purpose, a runner, and a one page report.

shot.visual_intent: A box labelled 'GitHub repo' opens; four parts rise out of it in turn: prompt page, bug block, runner server, report page.
shot.motion_claim: A box labelled 'GitHub repo' opens; four parts rise out of it in turn: prompt page, bug block, runner server, report page.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The tests will run against a small loan application API that I built earlier with Claude's help. It uses made up applicants and mock vendors, and it checks rules like a minimum income and the order of each step.

shot.visual_intent: A server stack labelled 'loan API' lights up; two rule tags clip onto it: 'min income', 'step order'.
shot.motion_claim: A server stack labelled 'loan API' lights up; two rule tags clip onto it: 'min income', 'step order'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: This part exists. On October twelfth, I ran it on made up applicants with Claude Code. An income of fourteen thousand, nine hundred and ninety nine rupees was rejected. Fifteen thousand got an offer. And paying out a loan before the earlier steps was refused. It has no tests yet.

shot.visual_intent: Three applicant cards ride up to the server one at a time: one gets an X, one a check, one a stop bar with '409'.
shot.motion_claim: Three applicant cards ride up to the server one at a time: one gets an X, one a check, one a stop bar with '409'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Here's the core idea. I break one rule on purpose. Say the minimum income drops from fifteen thousand to fifteen hundred. Then I run the tests again. If a test goes red, it bites. If everything stays green, the tests just missed a real bug.

shot.visual_intent: The rule block '15,000' is swapped for '1,500' with a spark; the test crate rides through a gate; one page flips to an X.
shot.motion_claim: The rule block '15,000' is swapped for '1,500' with a spark; the test crate rides through a gate; one page flips to an X.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: It works the other way too. A test that fails on the correct code means Claude got something wrong. Every one of those goes into a dated log, with how I caught it.

shot.visual_intent: A test page with an X on a green server; a quill writes lines onto a log page beside it.
shot.motion_claim: A test page with an X on a green server; a quill writes lines onto a log page beside it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: From their docs, Postbot generates test scripts, and Schemathesis checks an API against its schema. On October thirteenth, I ran Stryker on my loan rules with Claude Code. It made ninety two mutants, but none changed the fifteen thousand limit, and its one step order mutant deletes every guard at once. BiteCheck adds those business rule bugs, one at a time.

shot.visual_intent: Two closed boxes (docs only), the Stryker box with the hero number 92 and '0 change 15,000', then the open BiteCheck box with a rule page.
shot.motion_claim: Two closed boxes (docs only), the Stryker box with the hero number 92 and '0 change 15,000', then the open BiteCheck box with a rule page.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The reader is a hiring manager or engineer screening me for a new grad software or AI role. In the first minute, they run one command and read one page: did the tests pass on the real API, which bugs were caught, which survived, and where Claude was wrong.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal window types one command; a report page slides out with three bars growing.
shot.motion_claim: A terminal window types one command; a report page slides out with three bars growing.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: What would it show about me? First, a prompt contract: every test Claude writes must name the rule it checks. That's source grounding. A test that can't point to a rule gets thrown out.

shot.visual_intent: A rule page and a test page; a cable draws from the test to the rule; a test page with no cable drops into a bin.
shot.motion_claim: A rule page and a test page; a cable draws from the test to the rule; a test page with no cable drops into a bin.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Second, an agent loop with limits. Claude Code may edit the tests, never the API, and stops after a fixed number of tries. Third, evaluation: a score, plus every miss. It won't prove this works on every API. I'll measure it on one.

shot.visual_intent: A loop arrow circles between Claude's test pages and the runner; a lock clicks onto the API server; a score bar fills.
shot.motion_claim: A loop arrow circles between Claude's test pages and the runner; a lock clicks onto the API server; a score bar fills.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: What's out: it won't be a tool for any API, and it will never fix application code. What comes first: the income rule. One bug, run in GitHub Actions. You'll know it ran when a committed report shows the real API passing and that bug caught.

shot.visual_intent: A wrench over the API is crossed out; then a three-gate CI belt carries one bug block to a check.
shot.motion_claim: A wrench over the API is crossed out; then a three-gate CI belt carries one bug block to a check.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk is me. I write the bugs, so I could make them easy to catch without meaning to. So I'll commit the full bug list before Claude writes any test, and the git history will show the order. The report will list every bug that survived, not just the score.

shot.visual_intent: A timeline: the 'bugs' commit dot lands first with a lock, then the 'tests' dot; a survivors page slides out.
shot.motion_claim: A timeline: the 'bugs' commit dot lands first with a lock, then the 'tests' dot; a survivors page slides out.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? Mostly learning. I've done API testing and CI gates at my last job, but that work is private. What I can show is my public Reallocation Engine pull request, a Claude workflow with a run log. Mutation testing and evaluation design are new to me. Finding out how well Claude's tests do is the point.

shot.visual_intent: Two shelves: 'have' with two private blocks and one public PR block; 'new to me' with two outlined blocks.
shot.motion_claim: Two shelves: 'have' with two private blocks and one public PR block; 'new to me' with two outlined blocks.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object per beat on a cream stage; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: So, where it stands today. The loan API exists, and it ran. This brief and this film exist. Everything else, the prompt, the bugs, the tests, the runner and the report, is still to be built. This is BiteCheck. I'm Omkar Salian.
